signatures.doc: snipmd_core::paths. Percent-decodes the link, then accepts only a relative path that stays inside note_dir. Rejects: absolute (/x, C:\x), drive-relative (C:x), UNC (\\server\share, //server/share), any `..` that leaves note_dir, any `:` after decoding (NTFS streams, schemes), empty links, NUL, malformed percent-encoding (PathError::Invalid). Accepts both / and \ as separators. `./a.png` and `sub/../a.png` are fine. Returns note_dir joined with the cleaned relative path; purely lexical, no file system access.

signatures.signature: pub struct AllowedSet; pub fn new() -> Self; pub fn allow_note(&mut self, note: &Path); pub fn allow_dir(&mut self, dir: &Path); pub fn check(&self, p: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, PathError>
signatures.doc:
snipmd_core::paths. allow_note allows exactly that file plus its `<stem>.assets/` folder (recursive). allow_dir allows a folder recursively. check normalizes lexically (removes `.`, resolves `..`, unifies separators) and returns the normalized path when it equals an allowed file or lies inside an allowed folder; otherwise PathError::NotAllowed. Relative input is NotRelative. Comparison is case-insensitive on Windows (cfg(windows)) and exact elsewhere. `C:
otes\a.md` must not allow `C:
otes\a.md.evil` or `C:
otes-other\x`. No file system access, so a note that does not exist yet (Save As target) can be allowed.

signatures.doc: The open and save dialogs run in Rust (tauri_plugin_dialog::DialogExt, non-blocking pick with a oneshot channel). A picked path is added to the allowed set before it is returned. Filters: Markdown md/markdown for open, md for save.

Rust handles WindowEvent::DragDrop(Drop) in on_window_event, allows every dropped .md/.markdown path as a note, then emits `files-dropped` with all dropped paths. The frontend no longer uses onDragDropEvent.

The one path into the allowed set for a note: AllowedSet::allow_note (state: Mutex<AllowedSet> managed by Tauri) plus asset_protocol_scope().allow_directory(note's parent folder, true). At startup the app data folder is allowed the same way (allow_dir + asset scope). Callers: pick_open, pick_save, drop, get_cli_startup_files, the single-instance callback, load_session.
